description.value: Northern Sunrise Charters runs all-inclusive, multi-day boat charter adventures into the remote wilderness of BC's north coast, departing from the Nisga'a community of Gingolx near the Portland and Observatory Inlets. The fleet of four vessels—ranging from a 34' Double Eagle mothership to a 27' landing craft—supports fishing for salmon, halibut, and lingcod, plus wildlife viewing of grizzlies, orcas, humpbacks, and eagles. Captain George Alexcee brings 47 years of coastal experience, and chef Mary-Lee Alexcee, a lifelong Gingolx resident, provides gourmet meals from freshly caught seafood aboard.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website is fully accessible and provides detailed information about a boat charter operation based in Gingolx on BC's remote north coast. No cycling-specific amenities (bike parking, washrooms, water refill) are mentioned anywhere on the site. Gourmet meals are provided aboard the vessels as part of all-inclusive multi-day charters, not as a walk-in food service. The phone number '12509751466' appears prominently on the website header.
concerns: OSM record has no address, phone, or osm_id populated — only a lat/lon and manually supplied URL. Physical departure point appears to be Gingolx but is not explicitly confirmed in OSM tags.
No OSM phone to corroborate against; phone sourced from website header only.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Real, operating boat charter and wildlife tour business with an active website. Flagged always_include=true and represents a notable Indigenous-community-connected attraction on BC's remote north coast.
enrichment_extras.notes: This is a water-based charter operation; cyclist relevance is as a destination attraction (multi-day wilderness tour) rather than a service stop. The 'Pleasures in Paradise' page mentions accommodation at local B&Bs and a lodge in Gingolx, which may be of interest to touring cyclists in the area.
